key_insight: AlbumFill locates identity-consistent reference photos inside a user's album and uses them to guide a training-free image completion pipeline, enabling faithful, identity-preserving restoration without requiring explicitly provided references or model fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Restores occluded regions in personal photos while preserving the subject's identity and appearance, even when suitable reference images are not explicitly supplied.
method: Album-level retrieval: search the user's photo collection with identity-aware embeddings to find candidate reference images that match appearance and pose.
Reference reasoning & selection: rank and align the best matches, reasoning about which patches/attributes to borrow for the occluded area.

Training-free completion: condition an off-the-shelf inpainting/diffusion module on the selected references and perform compositing/latent blending to produce identity-consistent results without retraining.
impact: Enables practical, deployable personalized photo repair that doesn't require curated references or costly retraining, lowering engineering effort and improving user experience for photo editing and restoration tools.
visual_elements: Before/After gallery: target image with occlusion next to completed result highlighting preserved identity features (face/hair/clothing).
Pipeline flowchart: album retrieval → reference ranking/alignment → reference-conditioned inpainting (training-free) with short captions for each block.
Reference matching visualization: thumbnails of top-k retrieved album photos with similarity scores and alignment overlays on the target.
Evaluation snapshot: small bar chart or icons comparing identity-consistency and perceptual quality vs. baseline inpainting methods.
paper_title: AlbumFill: Album-Guided Reasoning and Retrieval for Personalized Image Completion
paper_authors: Yu-Ju Tsai, Brian Price, Qing Liu, Luis Figueroa, Daniil Pakhomov
